//: One person shipping software. Copy to ../org.config.json and edit the roots.

departments.name: Product
departments.mission: Ship and keep alive the things that charge money directly.
departments.note: Name the one event chain that tells you whether the product works. Instrumentation you never read is not instrumentation.

items.label: main-app
items.desc: The repo that makes the money.

items.label: payments
items.desc: Owns the path from checkout to activation.

items.label: github
items.desc: Repos, pull requests, issues, code search.

items.label: e2e-tests
items.desc: Browser tests against the running app.

items.label: incident-log
items.desc: Nothing records what broke, when, or what fixed it. Every outage is diagnosed from scratch.

items.label: analytics
items.desc: Product analytics for the funnel events.

items.label: scheduled-read
items.desc: Nobody reads the funnel on a cadence, so the link between a launch and a signup is never observed.

departments.name: Growth
departments.mission: Get the product in front of people who have the problem it solves.
departments.note: Launches are not a channel. Write down which channel actually brought signups, or you will relaunch forever.

items.label: attribution
items.desc: Nothing links a signup back to where it came from.

departments.name: Revenue
departments.mission: Charge correctly and keep the people who pay.
departments.note: Churn is a product problem wearing a finance costume. Log the reason, not just the number.

items.label: price-page
items.desc: Tiers, limits and what changed when.

items.label: churn-reasons
items.desc: Cancellations are counted but the reason is never captured.

departments.name: Memory
departments.mission: Hold the reasoning so you stop relitigating settled questions.
departments.note: Architecture arguments you have already had belong in decisions.md with an exit condition.

items.label: decision-log
items.desc: Why, and what would reverse it.
